reason: Conversation 1 answered the 'SA2' question correctly up front (model, not a fault code), asked the right diagnostic questions, had the customer isolate power before checking the fan by hand, and reached the correct diagnosis of a seized fan motor, matching the hidden truth. Conversation 2 never answered the SA2 question despite being asked twice, wasted the first turn on a clock-mode theory the opener didn't support, and then ended with a disproportionate 'stop using / fire risk' escalation triggered by a single transient hot smell, without ever diagnosing the seized motor. Conversation 1's weaknesses are that it defaulted to 'call an engineer' rather than offering the DIY motor swap the customer could do with power off, and it never got the full model from the rating plate for part sourcing, but it still clearly served the homeowner better.
